newsitem.title: MEXICO: Bancomext on verge of renewing commercial paper.
newsitem.headline: Bancomext on verge of renewing commercial paper.

text.p: Mexican development bank Bancomext is on the verge of announcing that it will renew its $300 million dollar commercial paper program for another year, a government official said on Monday.
"What we are doing is renewing the program for one year," the official told Reuters.

"We are putting together the documents, and we are expecting that in the next week, we can announce it," said the official, who declined to be further identified. The renewed commercial paper is seen yielding "LIBOR plus five-eighths," the official said.

Bancomext, Banco Nacional de Comercio Exterior, initiated its commercial paper program in the United States in January this year. It placed $300 million in commercial paper then at a rate of LIBOR plus 1.40 percentage points.
The lead agents for the renewal are Bank of America and Societe Generale. The existing U.S. dollar commercial paper program has an investment grade rating.

Bancomext, which promotes and finances foreign trade, has said that a good part of its financing for the next year would be in short-term loans and commercial paper. The development bank, Mexico's second largest, also has a Euro medium-term note program.
